headword: {不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}

definitions.explanation: The act of entering someone's property, building, or territory without permission or legal right. A legal term commonly seen in news reports.

examples.japanese: {不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}で{逮捕|たいほ}された。
{敷地|しきち}への{不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}を{防|ふせ}ぐためにカメラを{設置|せっち}した。
examples.english: Cameras were installed to prevent trespassing on the property.

examples.japanese: {深夜|しんや}に{学校|がっこう}に{不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}した{疑|うたが}いで、{男|おとこ}が{取|と}り{調|しら}べを{受|う}けている。
examples.english: A man is being questioned on suspicion of illegally entering a school late at night.

notes:
USAGE:
A legal and news term. In Japanese criminal law, this corresponds to {住居|じゅうきょ}{侵入|しんにゅう}{罪|ざい} (crime of trespass). Frequently seen in news reports about break-ins and unauthorized entry.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}する (to trespass)
- {不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}{者|しゃ} (trespasser)
- {不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}の{疑|うたが}い (suspicion of trespassing)
- {不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}で{逮捕|たいほ}される (to be arrested for trespassing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {侵入|しんにゅう}: intrusion, entry — neutral, can be legal or illegal
- {不法|ふほう}{侵入|しんにゅう}: specifically illegal entry
